source.title: Diversity is All You Need: Learning Skills without a Reward Function.

confidence_rationale: DIAYN formalises exactly the coupling Q-054 asks about: a discriminator q(z|s) can only separate latent classes to the extent the policy produces discriminable (diverse) behaviour, via the objective I(S;Z)=H(Z)-H(Z|S). This supports the EXISTENCE of a diversity->discriminability dependence (ARC-062 = the discriminator, ARC-065 = the diversity generator). It does NOT, however, quantify a minimum entropy FLOOR, which is the specific numeric Q-054 poses (is 0.497 nats enough?). Framework-level support, not a threshold measurement.
failure_signatures: DIAYN couples diversity and discriminability bidirectionally (the discriminator reward shapes the policy), so a fixed upstream entropy is not strictly required -- a caution that Q-054's 'static floor' framing may be ill-posed if the ARC-062 discriminator is allowed to shape the ARC-065 stream rather than read a frozen one.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Maximising the mutual information I(S;Z)=H(Z)-H(Z|S) between visited states and a latent skill index, via a learned discriminator q(z|s) plus a maximum-entropy policy, yields skills that are both diverse and distinguishable; minimising H(Z|S) means the skill must be easy to infer from the states it visits.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-062's reef/forage context discriminator is the analogue of q(z|s); the upstream first_action_entropy that ARC-065 must supply is the policy-entropy term. Q-054's 'discriminative cut' exists only when H(context|behavior) is drivable low, which requires the behavioural stream to be diverse enough -- precisely DIAYN's H(Z|S) term. The information-theoretic lower bound Q-054 cites (I(context;action)) is the DIAYN objective read in REE's vocabulary.
mapping.mapping_caveat: DIAYN learns the discriminator and policy JOINTLY toward a mutual-information optimum and never reports a critical entropy threshold below which discrimination fails; Q-054 wants a numeric floor on a (possibly fixed) upstream entropy. The paper supports the coupling and the lower-bound intuition but not the specific 0.497-nat sufficiency question -- that remains the empirical job of V3-EXQ-543b.
mapping.source_context: Continuous-control RL benchmarks (MuJoCo, etc.); unsupervised skill discovery; latent skills z.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational, well-cited; but it answers the QUALITATIVE coupling, not the quantitative floor Q-054 asks for -- mapping_fidelity deliberately mid, transfer risk from joint-trained skills to a fixed-stream discriminator is real.
